findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] app/views/embed/best.html.erb:6 — `<%- end if %>` is not valid Ruby (`end` cannot take a modifier `if`); the ERb template fails to compile with a SyntaxError, so every `/embed/best` request that finds a topic returns a 500 instead of rendering comments (controller specs never render views, so this isn't caught)

[High/security] app/models/post.rb:131 (with topic_embed.rb / poll_feed.rb / best.html.erb:19) — the new `raw_html` cook method stores external HTML as `cooked` with zero sanitization (PollFeed passes RSS `i.content` through completely unfiltered; the readability path filters tag/attribute names but not URL schemes, so `javascript:` hrefs survive), and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked` — a compromised/malicious feed or article yields stored XSS on both the embedding site and the forum

[High/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the feed-supplied `url` is interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` in the "imported from" footer; the only validation is the `^https?://` prefix check, so a link containing a single quote breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML/JS into the post

[Medium/security] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — `/embed/best` is unauthenticated and enqueues a `RetrieveTopic` job per request with an attacker-controlled, unbounded `embed_url`; the Referer gate is trivially forged by non-browser clients, and each novel URL on the embeddable host makes the worker run the entire PollFeed inline plus an HTTP fetch (topic_retriever.rb:41) — a cheap-request/expensive-work DoS amplification vector

[Medium/data] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — the PR edits an already-released migration, adding `force: true`, which drops the existing `top_topics` table (data loss) if the migration ever re-runs; already-migrated installs never receive the change (the whitespace-only edit to 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb is the same anti-pattern)

[Medium/bug] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31-36 — no per-item error handling in the items loop: one malformed item (nil `i.content` → NoMethodError, nil title → DB error on create, bad link) raises and aborts the whole run, and with `retry: false` all remaining items are skipped until the next hourly poll

[Medium/performance] db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, default: 1, null: false` forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PG < 11, which can lock the posts table for a long time on large production forums

[Medium/performance] lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 / topic_embed.rb#import_remote — `open(url)` is called with no timeout and no response-size cap, and `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a full feed download+parse inline inside the worker; a slow/hanging or huge feed/article ties up Sidekiq workers and can exhaust memory

[Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js + app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss — new standalone bundles are never registered in `config.assets.precompile` (no asset config changes anywhere in the diff); Rails only precompiles registered non-default bundles, so production will 404 the embed script and the iframe stylesheet

[Low/security] lib/topic_retriever.rb / app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote — `Kernel#open` is used on externally-influenced strings (including disqus-export links in lib/tasks/disqus.thor); `open("|cmd")` executes shell commands, so any path that bypasses the `URI()` host validation (e.g., the thor import path) is command-injectable — use `OpenURI`/`URI#open` instead

[Low/concurrency] lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is non-atomic; a crash between the two leaves the throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL

[Low/concurrency] app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-27 — check-then-create race on `embed_url`: two concurrent jobs can both pass the `embed.blank?` check, and the loser hits the unique index with an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (the transaction rolls back so no duplicate data, but the job errors out)

[Low/security] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js:17 — `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring containment check rather than strict origin equality, and `e.data.height` is used unvalidated; should compare the exact origin and validate the height is numeric

[Low/security] app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb:13 — `request.referer` is interpolated unescaped into inline JavaScript; use `j`/JSON encoding (currently only saved by the controller's `URI()` parse rejecting malformed referers)

[Low/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb#absolutize_urls — only leading-`/` URLs are rewritten; protocol-relative (`//host/...`) and bare-relative (`page.html`, `?q`) links are left as-is and resolve against the Discourse origin inside the iframe, breaking them

[Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no `render_views`, so the embed views (including the template syntax error and the `raw post.cooked` rendering) are completely untested; likewise poll_feed_spec only tests the settings guard, never the actual import logic

[Low/test_gap] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 — `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` is a copy-paste error (should require the poll_feed job); the spec only passes because jobs are eagerly loaded elsewhere
[Low/doc_defect] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — `feed_key` is dead code, never referenced anywhere (apparently an unfinished conditional-fetch/If-Modified-Since feature)

[Low/bug] app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7-10 — the page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal error state; when retrieval can never succeed (e.g., `embed_by_username` unset, host mismatch, feed disabled) clients poll indefinitely and keep re-enqueuing retrieve jobs

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/post.rb:131 (with topic_embed.rb / poll_feed.rb / best.html.erb:19) — the new `raw_html` cook method stores external HTML as `cooked` with zero sanitization (PollFeed passes RSS `i.content` through completely unfiltered; the readability path filters tag/attribute names but not URL schemes, so `javascript:` hrefs survive), and best.html.erb renders it with `raw post.cooked` — a compromised/malicious feed or article yields stored XSS on both the embedding site and the forum

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `raw_html` cook path that bypasses the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb). `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and sets `raw` to `absolutize_urls(url, contents)` where `contents` comes from external sources (RSS via Jobs::PollFeed uses `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` with no sanitization; TopicEmbed.import_remote uses Readability with allowed `href/src` attributes but no scheme validation). The embed view renders this with `raw post.cooked` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), so attacker-controlled HTML/attributes (e.g., `javascript:` URLs or other XSS vectors) can be stored and rendered. This is a verifiable stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 — the feed-supplied `url` is interpolated unescaped into `<a href='#{url}'>` in the "imported from" footer; the only validation is the `^https?://` prefix check, so a link containing a single quote breaks out of the attribute and injects arbitrary HTML/JS into the post

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the only check is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, then `url` is interpolated directly into `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. Since the newly added `cook_method == :raw_html` path in `Post#cook` returns `raw` verbatim (bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), an embed/feed URL containing a single quote can break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JS into the stored post content, which is later rendered with `raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:13 — `/embed/best` is unauthenticated and enqueues a `RetrieveTopic` job per request with an attacker-controlled, unbounded `embed_url`; the Referer gate is trivially forged by non-browser clients, and each novel URL on the embeddable host makes the worker run the entire PollFeed inline plus an HTTP fetch (topic_retriever.rb:41) — a cheap-request/expensive-work DoS amplification vector

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new public GET route `get 'embed/best' => 'embed#best'` and controller action `EmbedController#best` which, when no existing `TopicEmbed` is found, enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ..., embed_url: embed_url)` for a caller-supplied `embed_url` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The only gate shown is `ensure_embeddable`, which checks `request.referer` host against `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`—a header that is trivially forgeable by non-browser clients—and does not constrain `params[:embed_url]` beyond being present. The enqueued job executes `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, and for each novel URL on the allowed host it can run expensive work: `perform_retrieve` will call `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline when `feed_polling_enabled` is true, plus `fetch_http` which ultimately does `open(url).read` and Readability parsing (lib/topic_retriever.rb, app/models/topic_embed.rb). The throttling is per-URL (`retrieved:#{@embed_url}`), so an attacker can bypass it by varying the URL path/query to trigger repeated expensive processing. This is a verifiable DoS amplification risk introduced by the new embedding flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/data] db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb:3 — the PR edits an already-released migration, adding `force: true`, which drops the existing `top_topics` table (data loss) if the migration ever re-runs; already-migrated installs never receive the change (the whitespace-only edit to 20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb is the same anti-pattern)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does edit two existing migrations: it changes `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true` and makes whitespace/newline-only changes in `20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb`. Editing already-released migrations is a legitimate review concern because already-migrated installs won’t replay these changes, and `force: true` would drop/recreate the table if this migration were ever rerun (e.g., via redo on a DB where `top_topics` exists), risking data loss. However, on a normal forward-only migration path the change does not introduce an immediate defect (new installs won’t have the table yet), so this is more of a migration/process hazard than a guaranteed bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb:3 — `add_column :posts, :cook_method, default: 1, null: false` forces a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on PG < 11, which can lock the posts table for a long time on large production forums

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a migration `db/migrate/20131219203905_add_cook_method_to_posts.rb` with `add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`. Adding a NOT NULL column with a non-null DEFAULT can trigger a full table rewrite and long `ACCESS EXCLUSIVE` lock on older PostgreSQL versions, which is a real deployment/performance risk on large `posts` tables. This is not a functional bug in application logic, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded operational concern caused by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 and app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29 / topic_embed.rb#import_remote — `open(url)` is called with no timeout and no response-size cap, and `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs a full feed download+parse inline inside the worker; a slow/hanging or huge feed/article ties up Sidekiq workers and can exhaust memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces multiple unbounded network reads via `open-uri` without timeouts or size limits: `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` does `open(url).read`. Additionally, `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` synchronously (not enqueued), so a slow/hanging or huge feed/article fetch can block the calling Sidekiq job (`Jobs::RetrieveTopic`) and potentially exhaust memory while parsing/reading. This is a real reliability/performance defect grounded in the added code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] app/assets/javascripts/embed.js + app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss — new standalone bundles are never registered in `config.assets.precompile` (no asset config changes anywhere in the diff); Rails only precompiles registered non-default bundles, so production will 404 the embed script and the iframe stylesheet

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new top-level asset entrypoints `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss`. The new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` explicitly references the stylesheet via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'`, implying it must be compiled as its own bundle. However, the diff shows no change to any asset precompile configuration (e.g., `config/initializers/assets.rb` / `config.assets.precompile`). In typical Rails/Sprockets defaults, only `application.js`/`application.css` are precompiled, so standalone `embed.js`/`embed.css` would not be generated in production, leading to missing asset 404s for the iframe page (and for `embed.js` if it’s intended to be loaded externally).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/security] lib/topic_retriever.rb / app/models/topic_embed.rb#import_remote — `Kernel#open` is used on externally-influenced strings (including disqus-export links in lib/tasks/disqus.thor); `open("|cmd")` executes shell commands, so any path that bypasses the `URI()` host validation (e.g., the thor import path) is command-injectable — use `OpenURI`/`URI#open` instead

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `TopicEmbed.import_remote` which calls `open(url).read` on `url` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). That `url` can come from externally influenced data without host validation in the Disqus import task (`lib/tasks/disqus.thor` now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)`). `TopicEmbed.import_remote` performs no scheme/host checks before `open`, so a crafted value like a pipe-prefixed string could trigger `Kernel#open` command execution. While `TopicRetriever` does validate host for the embed controller path, the Thor import path bypasses it, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] lib/topic_retriever.rb:27-28 — `$redis.setnx` followed by a separate `$redis.expire` is non-atomic; a crash between the two leaves the throttle key with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb#retrieved_recently?, the code uses `$redis.setnx(retrieved_key, "1")` and then separately calls `$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`. If the process crashes or is killed after `setnx` succeeds but before `expire` runs, the key will be left without a TTL. Subsequent calls will see `setnx` fail and treat the URL as "retrieved recently" forever, permanently throttling retrieval for that embed URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/concurrency] app/models/topic_embed.rb:14-27 — check-then-create race on `embed_url`: two concurrent jobs can both pass the `embed.blank?` check, and the loser hits the unique index with an unhandled `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique` (the transaction rolls back so no duplicate data, but the job errors out)

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code does `embed = TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url).first` and then, if `embed.blank?`, enters a transaction and calls `TopicEmbed.create!(embed_url: url, ...)` (with a unique index on `topic_embeds.embed_url` added in the migration). Two concurrent callers importing the same `url` can both observe `embed.blank?` before either commit, and the loser will hit the unique constraint and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique`. There is no rescue/retry logic in the method or the calling jobs (`Jobs::PollFeed`, `TopicRetriever`), so the job/request can error out even though the DB prevents duplicates.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/models/topic_embed.rb#absolutize_urls — only leading-`/` URLs are rewritten; protocol-relative (`//host/...`) and bare-relative (`page.html`, `?q`) links are left as-is and resolve against the Discourse origin inside the iframe, breaking them

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, only `href`/`src` values that `start_with?('/')` are rewritten to absolute URLs. Other relative forms (e.g., `page.html`, `?q=1`, `#frag`) and protocol-relative URLs (`//cdn/...`) are left unchanged, despite the method comment stating it converts relative URLs to absolute. When this HTML is rendered inside Discourse (including in the embed iframe), those unchanged relative links will resolve against the Discourse origin instead of the source article, causing broken/incorrect URLs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — no `render_views`, so the embed views (including the template syntax error and the `raw post.cooked` rendering) are completely untested; likewise poll_feed_spec only tests the settings guard, never the actual import logic

adjudication.rationale: The new embed feature adds nontrivial view templates (e.g., `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` uses `<%= raw post.cooked %>`) and an embed layout with inline JS, but `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` is a controller spec without `render_views`, so it won’t exercise template rendering at all. Similarly, `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only asserts the settings guards and that `poll_feed` is invoked, but never tests the actual import behavior in `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` (SimpleRSS parsing, URL normalization, `TopicEmbed.import` calls). The mention of a specific “template syntax error” isn’t verifiable from the diff, but the broader untested-view/untested-import-logic gap is grounded in the added code/tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:2 — `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'` is a copy-paste error (should require the poll_feed job); the spec only passes because jobs are eagerly loaded elsewhere

adjudication.rationale: In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the file explicitly does `require_dependency 'jobs/regular/process_post'`, but this spec is for `Jobs::PollFeed` (new file app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). Nothing in the diff shows `process_post` being needed here, and the spec does not require the poll_feed job file, so the require looks like a copy/paste mistake that could make the spec depend on external eager loading rather than correctly loading the unit under test.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:20-22 — `feed_key` is dead code, never referenced anywhere (apparently an unfinished conditional-fetch/If-Modified-Since feature)

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` is defined (lines shown in diff: computes a Redis key using SHA1 of `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url`) but is never called from `execute`, `poll_feed`, or anywhere else in the provided diff. adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] app/views/embed/loading.html.erb:7-10 — the page reloads every 30 seconds forever with no terminal error state; when retrieval can never succeed (e.g., `embed_by_username` unset, host mismatch, feed disabled) clients poll indefinitely and keep re-enqueuing retrieve jobs

adjudication.rationale: The loading template unconditionally reloads every 30s (`app/views/embed/loading.html.erb`), and `EmbedController#best` enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` whenever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` is nil, then renders `loading`. There is no terminal error/stop condition, so the client will keep reloading indefinitely and repeatedly enqueueing retrieve jobs as long as no embed record is created. The diff also shows realistic “never succeeds” cases: `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` calls `SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` without guarding for nil/blank, so an unset `embed_by_username` can cause retrieval to fail while the loading page continues to reload/enqueue.
